transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration 52 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Ram, Carlos Mendes - Redwood; Aisha Thompson, Mark Ruiz, Eric Nguyen, Janelle Park - Skyline Technologies

Summary: Quick procurement/legal review covering the MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs (uptime/latency), pricing tiers and committed usage options, and next steps for a short dedicated pilot for benchmarking. Customer requests around audit logs, KMS, data residency and insurance limits.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll run through the MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing and a proposed pilot. Quick intros please.
00:08 Aisha Thompson: Hi, Aisha here, CPO at Skyline, I'm leading the vendor selection side from product.
00:12 Mark Ruiz: Mark, head of MLOps, I'll be driving the bench tests and infra requirements.
00:16 Eric Nguyen: Eric, procurement, here to track the process and timing.
00:19 Janelle Park: Janelle from legal, reviewing contract language.
00:22 Priya Ram: Priya, Redwood SE, I'll talk technical and run through SOC2/KMS stuff.
00:26 Carlos Mendes: Carlos, on solutions eng, happy to coordinate the pilot provisioning.
00:30 Jordan Lee: Great. First up, MSA redlines. Janelle, you sent a note earlier about retention and audit log retention — can you summarize?
00:41 Janelle Park: Sure, we asked for audit logs retained 7 years in our DPA and explicit encryption at rest with customer-managed keys. Also, limitation of liability cap is a concern — we'd like to see higher limits; also data residency to keep EU data in EU region.
00:58 Priya Ram: Okay, on KMS, Redwood supports KMS integrations — we do bring-your-own-key options with supported providers; we'll share the KMS integration guide. On retention, our default is 1 year but for enterprise contracts we can extend to 7 years but need to discuss storage cost impacts.
01:20 Mark Ruiz: Are those logs accessible via API for auditing? We need automated exports into our SIEM.
01:27 Priya Ram: Yes, we expose audit logs and can stream to your SIEM — there's a small throughput config that we can enable. I'll include the endpoint and an example in the runbook.
01:38 Eric Nguyen: On liability cap — what are typical limits? We've seen different numbers — some vendors do 2x MRR, others do $5M.
01:46 Jordan Lee: Typical Redwood enterprise deals land around $3M cap, but that can be negotiable depending on term and committed spend; we'll flag that for legal.
01:56 Janelle Park: We'll need a written proposal on that. Also indemnity language — we may want stronger carveouts.
02:05 Jordan Lee: Noted. Moving to SLAs: uptime and latency SLOs. For dedicated pool customers we offer an SLA for availability and target p99 latencies per model class. Priya, can you speak to the numbers?
02:18 Priya Ram: Sure. For dedicated we have a 99.9% availability SLA for serving nodes; for latency it depends on model family. For smaller Llama-ish models, typical p95 is sub-100ms on our T4-equivalent, p99 is more variable. For LLM-extended families and longer context, p99 can drift — we'll provide model-specific profile docs. For strict latency SLOs we recommend dedicated GPUs and pinning.
02:45 Mark Ruiz: Our SLO is p95 < 150ms for 512 tokens, and p99 < 350ms. Can Redwood commit to that on a pilot?
02:52 Priya Ram: We can aim to validate in the pilot; if you commit to a dedicated capacity tier we can usually meet p95 numbers. p99 is trickier, depends on batching and workload patterns. We'll run benchmarks with your sample traffic.
03:12 Carlos Mendes: For the pilot we'll need a representative traffic spec — burstiness, typical prompt lengths — Mark, can you share that?
03:20 Mark Ruiz: Yes, we'll export a week of traces and estimate token distributions. Expect spikes during business hours — roughly 30 req/s peak for the pilot profile.
03:30 Jordan Lee: Perfect. Pricing: Jordan to talk tiers and committed usage discounts.
03:33 Jordan Lee: For hosted API it's usage-based. For Dedicated and private, we do reserved capacity with monthly commits. Example: 3-month pilot dedicated plus 12-month reserved option gives stepped discounts — I'll attach the pricing worksheet. We can offer a preliminary discount if Skyline signs a 12-month commit after pilot.
03:52 Eric Nguyen: Procurement needs an itemized pricing sheet showing Opex vs Capex and any termination penalties. Also want clarity on change management cost if we scale up.
04:03 Jordan Lee: We'll provide a cost breakdown and example TCO for expected throughput; termination terms are in the MSA but we can propose a 30-day termination for pilot, standard notice for reserved.
04:12 Janelle Park: Can Redwood accept a mutual termination clause tied to SLA breaches?
04:18 Jordan Lee: We can take that back — typical is cure period and SLA credits; mutual termination for material breaches is something legal can review.
04:25 Priya Ram: Quick note on data residency — we can pin workloads to region, and for Private we can do on-prem or VPC with customer network controls. For EU-only residency we'll need to ensure the control plane access aligns with your needs.
04:42 Aisha Thompson: We need explicit language that EU customer data won't be routed through US systems.
04:47 Priya Ram: Understood — for the dedicated EU region we can ensure compute and storage remain in region; control plane metadata may need to be discussed. We'll include a diagram.
04:58 Mark Ruiz: What about MDS/MBR encryption and key rotation — how often do you rotate keys and is rotation customer-driven?
05:05 Priya Ram: KMS rotation is customer-driven; we support scheduled rotations and key versions. We'll share the KMS guide and sample rotation policy.
05:16 Jordan Lee: Insurance and SOC two — what's Redwood's posture?
05:19 Priya Ram: We have SOC 2 Type II, cyber liability $10M standard in enterprise contracts (can discuss higher with underwriting). I'll send the SOC2 report and a redacted pentest executive summary.
05:32 Janelle Park: Please send redlines and evidence.
05:35 Priya Ram: Will do.
05:38 Jordan Lee: On onboarding timeline — if legal clears, we can start pilot provisioning within 5 business days of the signed pilot agreement; bench tests within 48 hours of env access. Carlos will own setup.
05:49 Carlos Mendes: Yep, I'll coordinate. We have a provisioning checklist: infra access, keys, sample dataset, and test harness.
05:58 Mark Ruiz: For the pilot we need sample dataset confidentiality — can we do a synthetic dataset first?
06:05 Priya Ram: Absolutely. Synthetic first, then masked real data through a secure upload path. We also have a private S3 transfer option for PII.
06:16 Eric Nguyen: On approvals, procurement timeline at Skyline — we target an internal procurement approval by EoQ but hope to accelerate for this vendor.
06:25 Jordan Lee: Good — his target sign date? (some cross talk)
06:29 Aisha Thompson: We're aiming mid-April for a full signature, pilot to start early April if possible.
06:36 Jordan Lee: Ok, so next steps agreed: we'll send redlined MSA/DPA with proposed liability cap and data residency language; Priya will send SOC2/pentest/KMS docs; Carlos will prepare pilot provisioning doc; and Jordan will put together pricing workbook.
06:52 Janelle Park: One question on subcontractors — we need a list of hosting/subcontractors and subprocessor list for the DPA.
06:58 Priya Ram: We'll attach the subprocessor list (AWS, GCP partners, etc.) and highlight anything that touches data.
07:06 Mark Ruiz: Technical question — can you support KV cache separation per tenant? We need to ensure no cross-tenant leakage.
07:14 Priya Ram: Yes, per-tenant KV namespaces and strong isolation. It's part of our runtime design. I'll include architecture notes.
07:24 Aisha Thompson: Any regulatory concerns for finance data? We do have some regulated flows — need to confirm Redwood's compliance posture for financial services.
07:33 Priya Ram: We do work with regulated customers; we can discuss additional controls and a private deployment option for higher assurance.
07:40 Jordan Lee: Ok, time check, 40 minutes in. Any other blockers?
07:44 Eric Nguyen: One more: please confirm payment terms and invoice cadence — net 30 vs net 45 is a negotiation point.
07:50 Jordan Lee: We'll propose Net 30 standard but can do Net45 for enterprise with a slightly different pricing cadence — will note in the worksheet.
07:58 Carlos Mendes: Pilot checklist recap: access, keys, sample traces, benchmark script, expected SLO targets. I'll send a GDoc template.
08:08 Mark Ruiz: We'll fill that and include token distributions.
08:12 Janelle Park: Legal question — demo data retention after the pilot, how long is retained if we don't proceed?
08:18 Priya Ram: Demo data is removed after 30 days unless otherwise requested; we can align that with your DPA terms.
08:25 Aisha Thompson: Sounds good. Final recap please.
08:28 Jordan Lee: Recap: Redwood will send redlined MSA/DPA and pricing worksheet (Jordan), SOC2, pentest and KMS docs (Priya), pilot provisioning checklist (Carlos), Skyline to review and confirm procurement path (Aisha/Eric) and legal to review redlines (Janelle). Target legal-to-legal week of 2026-03-30. Pilot provisioning aimed early April. Any final comments?
08:55 Janelle Park: No, thanks we'll review the redlines.
08:59 Aisha Thompson: Thanks everyone.
09:02 Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the artifacts.

Notes: Transcript includes occasional quick cutoffs and minor transcription artifacts: e.g., p95/p99 occasionally rendered as p ninety-five. References to internal Redwood product names: "Dedicated" and "Private" were used; sometimes auto-transcription showed "private deployment" as "private deploy".

References shared during call: pricing worksheet (link: https://redwood.ai/pricing/CRM-789412-worksheet), SOC2 doc (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-redacted.pdf), KMS integration guide (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/kms-integration), pilot checklist (link: https://shared.redwood.work/pilot-checklist).

Action items (textual): Jordan to send pricing and MSA; Priya to send security docs; Carlos to provision pilot template; Skyline to confirm timelines.

End of transcript.
